resolutions.researcher_notes: This batch's KNOWN GOTCHA row: the wiki's only cited support was OPEC ASB2012 p.75, whose live opec.org link is dead. Recovered via Wayback (CDX-confirmed 200 capture); url_verifier OK on 'Libya'. Downloaded the capture and ran `pdftotext -layout` (url_verifier's substring check can't reach the compressed PDF text stream, matching the documented gotcha): Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Libya section, p.75, row 'Faregh/Intesar | Waha | 110 [mi] | 24 [in] | 7,080,147 [1,000 scm/yr] | na'. This is a specific, named match (not a generic country bulletin) and OPEC's dataset lists it as extant transport infrastructure carrying measured gas volumes in 2011 -- supports Status=operating (status is inferable from an operating-infrastructure listing, not a literal word match; see confidence_tiers.md convention). Second independent source: Waha Oil Company's own official website (wahaoil.ly, Arabic, archived via Wayback since the live site is behind a Cloudflare bot-check) lists 'حقل الفارغ' (Al-Faregh field) among its currently-operated field assets with coordinates (28.165343, 21.231562) in the same Sirte Basin corridor -- confirms the Faregh end of this line is a live Waha operating asset as of the 2023 snapshot, 12 years after the OPEC data point, independently corroborating continued operating status. Two independent origins (OPEC statistical body vs. Waha's own corporate site) -- tier high.

Same recovered Wayback ASB2012 capture, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75, manually confirmed via pdftotext given the PDF's compressed text stream defeats url_verifier's substring check). The 'Faregh/Intesar' row sits specifically within this gas-pipeline table (as opposed to Table 4.11, the separate petroleum-product-pipeline table with an entirely different Libya roster a few pages later), so Fuel=Gas is definitional to which table the row appears in. Single source; did not find a second independent source explicitly naming this pipeline's fuel type. tier medium.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012 (see Status notes), Table 4.10, Libya section, row 'Faregh/Intesar | Waha': Capacity column = 7,080,147 (units: 1,000 scm/yr per the table's column header) = 7,080,147,000 scm/yr = 7.080147 bcm/y -- an exact match to the sheet's value ('7.08') to 3 significant figures (7.080147 rounds to 7.08). This precision strongly indicates this is the sheet's original source data point. Single source; no independent second source found stating this specific pipeline's capacity figure by name (searches for 'Faregh' / 'Farigh' pipeline outside GEM/OPEC returned nothing relevant, and this session had no web-search budget remaining -- see overall notes on search-tooling constraints). tier medium.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012, Table 4.10, Libya, 'Faregh/Intesar | Waha' row: Length column = 110 (miles) = 177.03 km (110 x 1.609344) -- matches the sheet's LengthKnown value ('177.00' km) essentially exactly (rounding of the mile-to-km conversion). This is a very close numeric match confirming the row identity. Single source; no second independent source found giving this specific pipeline's length. tier medium.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012, Table 4.10, Libya, 'Faregh/Intesar | Waha' row: Diameter column = 24 (inches) -- exact match to the sheet's value ('24.00', DiameterUnits='in'). Single source; no independent second source found stating this specific pipeline's diameter. tier medium.

Country-level value only (Start/EndCountryOrArea = Libya, no sub-national detail in the brief). Two independent sources agree: (1) recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists 'Faregh/Intesar' under the 'Libya' section header. (2) Waha Oil Company's own official website (archived Wayback capture of wahaoil.ly, in Arabic) lists 'حقل الفارغ' (Al-Faregh field) with GPS coordinates 28.165343, 21.231562 -- squarely within Libya's Sirte Basin. Trivial/low-information fact but genuinely corroborated by two unrelated origins (an industry statistics body and the operator's own corporate site) -- tier high per the mechanical rule.

Operator='Waha Oil Co' (Arabic: شركة الواحة للنفط) confirmed by four independent sources: (1) recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists Owner/Operator = 'Waha' for the exact 'Faregh/Intesar' row (2011 data). (2) NOC's own official affiliated-companies page (noc.ly, verified live -- url_verifier OK) lists Waha Oil Company, with the Arabic name شركة الواحة للنفط matching the brief's OperatorLocalLanguage verbatim. (3) Waha Oil Company's own official site (archived, wahaoil.ly, Arabic) independently confirms the company name and lists 'Al-Faregh field' as one of its own operated assets, tying the operator directly to this pipeline's namesake field. (4) A Total S.A. SEC filing (EX-99.5 to a 2019 Form 6-K, an official Total press release dated 10 Dec 2019 titled 'Libya: Agreement Between NOC and Total Endorsing the Group's Entry into the Waha Concessions') states verbatim: 'The NOC (59.18%), Total (16.33%), ConocoPhillips (16.33%) and Hess (8.16%) jointly own the Waha concessions. Waha Oil Company, wholly owned by NOC, operates the asset.' NOTE on this SEC URL: url_verifier reports HTTP 403 because SEC.gov blocks the tool's default User-Agent as an 'undeclared automated tool' (SEC's fair-access policy requires a UA identifying the requester/contact, not a paywall) -- manually re-fetched with a declared UA (`curl -A 'pipelines-researcher research@globalenergymonitor.org'`), got HTTP 200, and confirmed the exact string 'NOC (59.18%), Total (16.33%), ConocoPhillips (16.33%) and Hess (8.16%)' present in the page text; this is the documented 'bot-wall false negative' pattern from the verifier's own docstring, not evidence the page is dead. Four independent origins (OPEC, NOC, Waha itself, Total/SEC) -- tier high.

Owner percentages (NOC 59.18%, ConocoPhillips 16.33%, TotalEnergies 16.33%, Hess 8.16%) match EXACTLY, verbatim, a Total S.A. SEC filing: EX-99.5 to a Form 6-K (filed 2019-12-31, accession 0001193125-19-326321), an official Total press release dated 10 Dec 2019, which states: 'The NOC (59.18%), Total (16.33%), ConocoPhillips (16.33%) and Hess (8.16%) jointly own the Waha concessions.' (Found via SEC EDGAR full-text search API, efts.sec.gov, which is not the blocked WebSearch tool -- a plain HTTPS GET against SEC's own search index.) On the url_verifier 403 for this live sec.gov URL: see the note under Operator -- SEC blocks the tool's default UA as an undeclared bot; manually verified 200 + exact-string match with a declared UA per SEC's documented fair-access policy. Independent second source: Marathon Oil Corp's own FY2018 Form 10-K (accession 0000101778-19-000022, filed 2019-02-21) states it 'closed on the sale of our subsidiary, Marathon Oil Libya Limited, which held our 16.33% non-operated interest in the Waha concessions in Libya... to a subsidiary of Total S.A. (Elf Aquitaine SAS) for proceeds of approximately $450 million' -- independently corroborates the 16.33% Total/ex-Marathon stake from the seller's side (a different corporate filer than Total). Cited via a Wayback capture of this SEC filing (timestamp 20240706005956), which passes url_verifier directly (OK, 200, contains '16.33'). Two genuinely independent origins (Total S.A. and Marathon Oil Corp, both primary corporate/regulatory disclosures, on opposite sides of the same transaction) -- tier high. This is a strong, precise resolution for a unit that a companion Libya row (P1857, 103D/103A) left UNRESOLVED for lack of a percentage-level source -- worth flagging to the batch as a reusable Owner reference for any other Waha-concession pipeline (Waha/Nasser, etc.) in this sweep.
